config.title: Write a function to sort objects by multiple keys

intro.title: Write a function to sort objects by multiple keys
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that sorts an array of objects based on multiple properties, such as sorting people by age and then by name. You will learn how to use the `Array.sort()` method with a custom comparator function that compares values sequentially. The main constructs involved are JavaScript arrays, objects, conditional logic, and comparison operators. By the end, you'll be able to sort complex data structures efficiently and understand the logic behind multi-key sorting.
intro.usecase: Sorting objects by multiple keys is essential for organizing complex data in real-world applications. In e-commerce dashboards, you might sort products by price (primary) and rating (secondary) to display best-value items. Customer relationship management systems often sort contacts by last name, then first name for organized directories. Data analytics tools use multi-key sorting to rank metrics by multiple dimensions, like sorting sales data by region then by revenue. This pattern appears whenever users need hierarchical organization of tabular data or ranked lists.

objectives: Implement a function that sorts an array of objects by a single property
Construct a comparator function that handles multiple sorting keys
Apply the localeCompare method for sorting string properties
Manipulate the sort order by specifying ascending or descending directions
Integrate the comparator function with the native array sort method
Initialize a sample dataset to test the multi-key sorting function
Render a sorted array of objects in the console to verify the output

steps.hint: Start with either 'function sortObjectsByKeys(arr, keys) {' or 'const sortObjectsByKeys = (arr, keys) => {'. Make sure to include the function body with a placeholder return statement.

steps.title: Handle ascending/descending sort order
steps.instruction: Inside the for loop, check if the current sort key starts with '-' to determine descending order. If it does, strip the '-' prefix and compare b[key] with a[key] (instead of a[key] with b[key]) to reverse the sort order.
steps.hint: You can use string methods like startsWith() and slice() to check for and remove the '-' prefix from the key.
steps.expectedOutcome: The compare function now handles both ascending (default) and descending (indicated by '-') sort orders for each key.
successCriteria: The code checks if the sort key starts with '-', strips it if present, and compares values with reversed order for descending sorts.
